newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks close higher, defector news ignored.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks close higher, defector news ignored.

text.p: Stocks closed higher on Thursday, though gains from ample liquidity were eroded by late profit taking, brokers said.
They said news of a high-ranking North Korea defector had little impact on trading.
The composite index closed 4.21 points higher at 716.71.

"Investors, especially institutions, tried to realise profits towards the close," said Jeon Jeong-tak of Hyundai Securities. "As we predicted, the 720 level posed a strong resistance." Brokers said sentiment remained unbeat despite late consolidation.
Seoul's Foreign Ministry said on Wednesday a close aide to North Korean leader Kim Jong-il was seeking asylum at South Korea's embassy in Beijing.
Shares of semiconductor companies soared in early afternoon trading on expectations of a business recovery, brokers said.
Samsung Electronics, the world's leading memory chip maker, rose 2,700 won to 59,000. It briefly hit its daily upper-limit of 60,800.
On Wednesday U.S. research firm Dataquest reported that the worldwide dynamic random access memory market was showing signs of rebounding from last year's oversupply.
